summary: Standard chess vs Stockfish with a neutral cognitohazard, the Boiled One (Doctor Nowhere), on b4. After both sides move, it steps one square orthogonally (random). Any piece of either colour that attacks/sees its square becomes permanently paralyzed for the rest of the game (cannot move, shown red). The Boiled One itself cannot capture and pieces cannot capture it [inferred]. Narrator shields his queen's diagonals, lets engine pieces stare at it, and wins.
rules: Standard chess otherwise; player White vs Stockfish (3600).
Neutral Boiled One starts on b4; after both White and Black have moved it moves one square orthogonally (random among empty squares).
It cannot capture; it cannot move onto occupied squares [inferred from 'shouldering' it with pawns].
Any piece that attacks the Boiled One's square (sees it along its movement/attack lines, pawns diagonally) becomes paralyzed for the rest of the game.
Paralyzed pieces cannot move; they presumably still block and can be captured [inferred]; whether they still give check is not stated.
Paralysis is checked after each move/its move (both a piece moving into line and the Boiled One stepping into a line trigger it).
